title: Summer 2024 Thermal Extremes & Heatwave Severity in Bengaluru
question: What were the highest recorded temperatures, which month experienced peak heat, and how many days exceeded 30°C daily mean?
interpretation: During the notable April–May 2024 South Indian heatwave, Bengaluru experienced unusually severe temperatures. The peak daily mean reached 32.38°C on 2024-04-18. A total of 23 days registered mean temperatures at or above 30.0°C.

title: Monsoon Precipitation Distribution and Extreme Rainfall Events
question: How was precipitation partitioned between South-West and North-East monsoon, and what was the single wettest day?
interpretation: Bengaluru received 938.76 mm of cumulative rainfall in 2024. The South-West Monsoon contributed 448.91 mm (47.8%), while the North-East retreat monsoon delivered 370.25 mm. The wettest day occurred on 2024-08-12 with 73.08 mm in 24 hours.

title: Humidity-Temperature Dynamics and Perceived Thermal Discomfort Index
question: How does Relative Humidity influence thermal comfort, and on which dates did the highest Thom Discomfort Index occur?
interpretation: The highest perceived discomfort peaked at 26.86°C on 2024-05-03, combining 32.08°C with 46.05% relative humidity. Monsoon air sat at high average humidity (79.8%), significantly modifying the physiological sensation of ambient heat.

title: Climatological Spell Analysis: Prolonged Dry Spells vs Wet Streaks
question: What was the longest consecutive rainless period versus continuous precipitation streaks in Bengaluru?
interpretation: Bengaluru experienced a severe pre-monsoon dry spell of 93 consecutive rainless days extending from 2024-01-10 through 2024-04-11, leading to city-wide groundwater stress. In contrast, the longest continuous rainy spell spanned 24 consecutive days during the peak monsoon.

title: Cross-System Big Data Performance Profiling (Hive Formats & MongoDB Indexes)
question: How do columnar storage (RCFile) and B-Tree indexing accelerate analytics compared to row text and full collection scans?
interpretation: Columnar RCFile reduced Hive query execution time by 52.4% (2.1x speedup) and compressed disk usage by 66.0% through column projection skipping. In MongoDB, compound indexing yielded a 7.82x speedup by eliminating full collection scans.
